text:
Jared Kim: Heads-up — AstraMed opened a dispute: they were charged a reserved commit prorate plus a vendor acceleration surcharge for the same GPU-hours in Mar (INV-2026-03-211). They say this is double-billing.
Mina Alvarez: pulled invoice extract: 
```
Line 14: Reserved capacity - AstraMed - 0.9 GPU-month = $10,800
Line 37: Reserved adjustment - decommit 0.3 (Mar10-31) prorate credit = -$3,600
Line 59: Vendor acceleration surcharge (partner premium) - 12 GPU-hrs = $1,560
Line 80: Burst overage - 6 GPU-hrs = $720
Invoice total: $9,480
```
Omar Rashed: event log shows on Mar10 we borrowed partner nodes to handle a failover and also rebalanced reserved pools same window. The partner surcharge was applied automatically for borrowed hours, but it looks like some of those hours overlapped with the prorated period where reserved capacity was decommitted.
Jared Kim: customer sent SUP-6572 saying they requested reserve reduction but the request processed after the failover. Their email timestamps: change request 2026-03-10T03:05Z; failover began 2026-03-10T02:58Z.
Mina Alvarez: policy: partner acceleration is an explicit pass-through for ad-hoc borrowing. Reserved prorate is separate. If the borrowing was caused by our infra event (not customer-initiated), partner pass-through should be refund-eligible.
Omar Rashed: vendor-relations — can you confirm whether partner billed us for those 12 hrs and whether they consider them chargeable given our agreed SLO?
vendor-relations: partner invoiced pb-123 for 12.0 hrs on 2026-03-11. Partner acknowledges some hours were due to our node failure and requested we submit evidence for credit.
Jared Kim: propose split adjustment: 1) reverse the prorate if the customer's change request preceded the decommit, OR if race, convert to transfer; 2) refund partner surcharge for hours caused by our failure; 3) reevaluate burst classification. Quick preliminary calc: reverse prorate credit (-$3,600) + waive partner surcharge (-$1,560) + adjust burst (-$360) -> net customer credit ~$1,920.
Mina Alvarez: need artifacts: SUP-6572, partner invoice, autoscale logs, customer change-email. @billing-bot create ADJ-2026-4999 and attach files. Flag discretionary > $1,000 for lead review.
billing-bot: Adjustment request ADJ-2026-4999 created. Artifacts attached: SUP-6572, partner-pb-123-invoice.pdf, autoscale-03-10.log, customer-change-email.pdf. Status: pending_lead_review.
Omar Rashed: vendor-relations — please open vendor dispute PD-245 and ask partner to provisionally credit the surcharge while we resolve.
vendor-relations: PD-245 opened with partner. Partner requested autoscale logs and we provided them. They indicated tentative credit pending review.
Mina Alvarez: finance lead required for discretionary > $1,000 — @billing-bot please tag Nadia for review.
billing-bot: ADJ-2026-4999 assigned to Nadia Chen for discretionary approval.
Jared Kim: I'll draft the customer comms offering the net credit and note that we're pursuing partner recovery. Tone: apology, one-time credit, partner recovery in process.
Mina Alvarez: also recommend product add a rule to avoid simultaneous autoscaler rebalances during manual commit changes (debounce + in-flight flag). Logging this as PR-612.
Omar Rashed: thanks — will follow up on PD-245 and post vendor status in ADJ-2026-4999.
vendor-relations: partner responded: provisional credit approved for 9 of 12 hrs; they will invoice us back for 3 hrs. That reduces our cost hit and increases approved customer credit.
billing-bot: ADJ-2026-4999 status updated: awaiting_nadia_decision.
Jared Kim: pinging Nadia for quick sign-off.
Nadia Chen: reviewed artifacts, approve discretionary credit $1,920. Please schedule for next billing run and create JE-2026-8123.
billing-bot: ADJ-2026-4999 status updated: approved_by_finance_lead. Scheduled for billing run 2026-04-03. Journal JE-2026-8123 created. Customer notified.
Mina Alvarez: closing loop: partner refunded most surcharge, customer credited $1,920, product ticket PR-612 opened. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
